purpose: Maps each Deque issue slug cited by the 16 page state tests to the one manual issue catalog entry a skill file branch should file. Hand-mapped: the two vocabularies do not join, and a success criterion names a family rather than an entry.
howToUse: Look the branch’s issue slug up here and file catalogOptionText verbatim into the Add Manual Issue combobox. The full option text — label and parentheses together — is the only unique key; the instance id inside it is not. A row resolves per branch, not per slug: where a slug is cited under more than one success criterion the row carries byCriterion and the branch’s own criterion selects the entry; where a slug is cited by two branches that mean different things under the same criterion the row carries byBranch and the branch selects directly. A row carries exactly one of catalogOptionText, byCriterion or byBranch.
byBranch: Keyed by a short branch name. Each cell carries the checklist condition it serves in `when`, copied verbatim from page-state-tests.json, which is what lets the check assert that the branch rows and the checklist branches are the same set. `semantic-data-table`’s branch names are check_table_semantics’ leaf names, so a skill file’s routing table and the mapping use one vocabulary.

confidence.high: the entry is an unambiguous match for the branch, under the criterion the checklist cites
confidence.low: flagged for a human: several entries in the family match equally, no entry matches well, or the closest entry sits under a different success criterion. Read the note before filing.

countsNote: counts rolls a slug up across its branches — a slug is low if any branch of it is. branchCounts is the per-branch tally over the 103 branches the checklist cites, which is what the completeness assertion covers.

mouse-keyboard-parity.note: The entry that matches the slug's name, kept for the branch it half-describes: an element that answers the mouse and the keyboard differently is behaving as if it had two roles. "Function cannot be performed by keyboard alone" (2.1.1.a) is closer for the keyboard-unavailable half, but it reports a success criterion the checklist does not cite here and says nothing about the mouse-unavailable half. A human should pick per finding.

aria-practices.when: the element is a known widget type (accordion, button, checkbox, disclosure, link, listbox, menu, menu bar, radio button or group, slider, spinbutton, toolbar control, tooltip trigger, window splitter) and its keyboard interactions do not follow the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices for that type
aria-practices.catalogOptionText: Custom user interface component is not compatible with AT (4.1.2.c)
aria-practices.note: The closest entry, and under the criterion the checklist cites, but it names incompatibility with assistive technology rather than departure from the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices' keyboard pattern — a widget can follow neither and still be announced correctly. Nothing in the catalog names the Authoring Practices. A human should confirm before filing.
